reason: UX-01: three undecided surfaces (publish flow, registrations vs check-in, save confirmation) and one container style needed Ivan's pick. The working method was a dev-only specimen route with labelled options, a recommendation, and verification at desktop, 375 px and dark. Nothing existing covers a design-options round, so it is new, born at class level for any undecided frontend surface.
Ivan approved the recommended UX-01 option but rejected the table's all-round border. The skill had no rule for partial picks, and table borders were not recorded as a preference.

Ivan asked the assistant to double-check that the chosen frontend component was actually applied. The first specimen used real Button/StatusPill but re-typed look-alike dialog, draft card and toolbar from product class strings, so the round showed designs the product would not render. The skill needs a fidelity rule.

The first specimen round copied product class strings instead of importing the real primitives. The user had to ask for a recheck. The rule was present but had no concrete check, so the grep makes it executable.

Browser pane probe read first-paint colours, so review item M4 (dark /pricing Choose buttons) looked like a contrast defect but was a measurement artefact. The specimen skill is where contrast numbers get put in front of Ivan, so the rule belongs here.

In the UX-02 round the specimen scrim was typed from memory (/40) and only matched to the product's Dialog primitive (/60) after a grep, and the dark-scheme veil was noticed late. The skill requires real primitives but does not say to copy overlay classes from the primitive or to check overlays in dark scheme.

The UX-02 round tried to open the preview pane with show_pane; the tool reported the session was in no window and left the view alone. The round still needs the reviewer to find the specimens, so the reply has to carry the route itself. The skill does not cover this case.

Episode: the UX-02 specimen round (7 sets, 21 options) was committed, then a 2026-10-30 two-persona doctrine fixed a different attendee nav. The specimens still drew the old labels, and the handoff had to flag that sets 1, 3 and 5 describe a nav that will not ship. The skill has no step that compares a round with the newer doctrine before a pick.

Motion options were first described as prose only; the round became checkable once a live switch existed. The builder then verified each mode by reading CSS animation names in the browser, which is the proof that the options differ. Make that the standard for motion specimens.

Ivan rejected a compressed 1f card because a full-width action row spilled into the date column. Layout fixes on specimen cards must keep the date column clear, and height claims need a before/after measurement.

Mid-iteration on a specimen tweak, the assistant launched lint, tsc and a multi-width sweep before Ivan had judged the frame. Ivan interrupted and redirected the layout instead. Verification should follow his visual sign-off during iteration.

Ivan asked for alignment checked with the frontend skills. The episode's checks only passed after measuring rects on a reloaded tab, and a skill-driven gap failure (touch targets 4 px apart) was caught only by measuring. The specimen skill should point at that measurement step.

Session needed several rounds on one card: date column width, tick box placement, height compression, then alignment. The Card 4 reference was a licensed block; the user had to correct the agent that it was not asking for a copy. These are durable rules for specimen rounds.

In the UX-02 re-cut the intro note contradicted option 5a and was fixed only because the assistant re-read its own copy; the card doc also needed a single live status after the re-cut. Both are round-hygiene steps the skill does not state.

Ivan's standing rule (2026-11-19): for all frontend changes, show the render first, not only for option picks. The skill was scoped to picks, so a mechanical or motion change could ship unrendered. Widened the trigger and added the render-first rule at the top of the body. This also overrides the MECHANICAL "just do it" track in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md for rendering: a mechanical change still gets a before/after render before any edit.

Companion to the trigger widening: the render-first rule needs its own body line so a reader who stops at the first lines still sees it. It also states the split between mechanical and decision changes, which the locked pipeline in CLAUDE.md does not make clear for rendering.

Episode built a dev-only S1 specimen. It loaded design-taste-frontend, then dropped it with a prose note instead of the ≥3-option conflict round CLAUDE.md requires. The lint-silencing sed insert failed on macOS and the agent fell back to Edit. Both are gaps in this skill's specimen-round guidance.

Episode S1/T1 pick application: Ivan approved picks, the assistant applied them. Contrast was re-measured before/after, a feature measured zero gain and was dropped, and a locked FDS hex change was flagged. The specimen skill has no rule for any of these steps.

Ivan's 2026-11-20 rule ("show me in live from here on out", "Yes, apply live") retires the old render-before-edit sketch step for single fixes. This skill still said widget-style before/after before any edit, so it contradicted the newer rule. Reconciled: options still use the specimen route; single fixes apply live then show frames.
Fold the narrow frontend consistency sweep into the specimen-round umbrella (same approval gate: read, draft batch, apply only on Ivan's word). Sibling deleted after this lands.
Add the consistency-sweep subsection absorbed from frontend-consistency-sweep.

Episode proposed then removed the public event page QR block. The reusable lessons: trace the target and shared helper callers before removal, show frames before applying, clean imports and mocks, and reset the viewport after the walk.
Ivan rejected a copy change to RegisterCard.tsx ("no need"). The assistant reverted it and proved the revert with an empty git diff. That check is the durable rule: a rejected edit leaves no diff.

The episode's frontend edits (nav CSS, a form line, a QR removal) were judged mechanical and never matched this skill's trigger, so it was not loaded before editing. The trigger must cover any Eventar frontend edit so the render-first path runs.

Ivan has repeated that frontend work must show the render, and this path (b) let the assistant apply first and show the render after. The render-first order must be explicit in the skill. The mechanical-change allowance in CLAUDE.md still applies to whether a change needs the pipeline, not to whether the render comes first.

Ivan asked on 2026-11-20 to always see frontend edits. The nav fix was reported as text, and the frames only went out after he complained. This rule makes SendUserFile delivery of before and after frames part of closing every frontend edit, even a one-class fix.

Ivan had to repeat the standing rule: a frontend choice was put to him as text with no before/after frames. The fix was a throwaway prototype rendered and reverted before asking. Procedure belongs in the skill that governs option picks, not only in global memory.

Ivan repeated the render rule on 2026-11-21: decision renders must be interactive Artifacts with live controls, and screenshots are proof-of-edit only. This skill still described the dev-route frames as the decision surface, so an agent following it would send screenshots.

Two concrete failures this episode: a specimen whose "before" read a live class so the diff vanished, and an artifact link sent before its controls were tested. Both are checks an agent following the skill would skip. Pinning the before and exercising controls are durable rules for every decision round.

Ivan's 2026-11-21 hero round: the assistant's first simulated-before and fix both looked applied, but the computed font-size had not changed. The simulation method needs a computed-value check and a caption naming it simulated.

Ivan's 2026-11-21 correction: "if i have approved then push, still pending then show me for approval." Pending rows were still open while approved rows went out, so the push rule needs to name pending rows explicitly.

Episode applied the edits first, then sent after-only frames and wrote zz-*.png into the repo root. Ivan's standing rule needs a before frame first; a patch must make the HEAD-worktree before the default when the edit already landed.
